summary.text: The candidates with the strongest convergent evidence are CA9, CD70, NNMT, COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) and SCARB1. Each is more abundant in tumour than in normal kidney in the CPTAC discovery cohort, the change is reproduced in TCGA-KIRC, and it survives extrapolation to a pure tumour, so it is carried by tumour cells rather than by infiltrating cells. CA9, CD70 and ENPP3 are surface antigens with clinical-stage antibodies or conjugates; NNMT is the one candidate where tumour expression, literature and TCGA survival agree on adverse prognosis; SCARB1 tops the target profile but carries a vital-organ safety flag and has no literature support in the corpus.

CA9 is the strongest single candidate. Its protein rises in tumour [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.269], the increase replicates in TCGA [gene=CA9; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=9.712], and RCC cells carry almost all of its tumour transcripts [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976]. It is a diagnostic, imaging and delivery target rather than a prognostic marker or a dependency: TCGA shows no survival association, and its protein is tissue-enriched in stomach [gene=CA9; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=5.19], which is the main safety concern for cytotoxic CA9 agents.

On the biomarker side the most robust calls are lost proximal-tubule and metabolic genes. PSAT1, PCK1 and SLC6A19 are stable at the top of the biomarker profile under random re-weighting, and their protein loss replicates in the independent confirmatory CPTAC cohort. ALDOB and ALDH6A1 are lost from tumour and their remaining expression tracks better survival in TCGA, so they are prognostic tissue-loss markers. None of these lost genes can be inhibited, so they are biomarkers only.

Two little-studied genes from the discovery screen are identified and prioritised for experimental validation. COL23A1, a transmembrane collagen, is made mainly by tumour cells [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881], replicates in TCGA and survives the purity extrapolation, with low vital-organ expression and no clinical drug; what is missing is a confirmed surface location (UniProt places it at the membrane, but surfaceome resources do not), normal-tissue staining, a selective dependency and data on heterogeneity across tumour cells, so immunohistochemistry on ccRCC and normal tissue arrays plus knockdown in 3D or in vivo models would test it. RAB42, a small GTPase, is also tumour-cell derived [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627] and replicates in TCGA, but it is intracellular, has no selective dependency and no survival signal, so it needs functional knockdown before any target claim. The strongest immune-track genes, MILR1 and LILRB4, are macrophage genes whose bulk increase comes from infiltration. Novel here means few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug; the analysis does not show that acting on any of these genes would help a patient.

Several independent layers return negative results that limit the target claims. None of the leading candidates is a selective DepMap dependency in ccRCC cell lines; EPAS1 is the only gene with a positive selectivity signal, consistent with approved belzutifan, and 2D cultures miss HIF-2 biology. No gene separates the treatment arms of IMmotion150 or CheckMate-025 after correction. HK2, despite ranking in the target top ten, does not replicate at the protein level in the confirmatory cohort.

omics.text: CD70 protein is up in tumour [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.421], the increase replicates in TCGA and survives the purity extrapolation, and the protein shows no enrichment in vital organs in the GTEx proteome [gene=CD70; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=0.34]. That makes it a cleaner surface target than CA9 on the normal-tissue axis, although the GTEx proteome has no kidney.

NNMT protein is strongly up in tumour [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.709], the change is tumour-intrinsic and replicates in TCGA, and higher expression predicts worse overall survival [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301]. It is a prognostic biomarker and a metabolic target candidate, but it is cytosolic and has no approved drug.

ALDOB marks the loss of proximal-tubule identity: its protein is down in tumour [gene=ALDOB; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-2.273], and lower expression is associated with worse survival in TCGA [gene=ALDOB; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.358]. It is a diagnostic or prognostic marker, not a target. ALDH6A1 behaves the same way and has the strongest favourable prognostic association in the biomarker shortlist.

VHL is the disease mechanism rather than a target: the short arm of chromosome 3 is lost in most tumours [gene=VHL; type=omics_cnv; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; loss_freq=0.791], with significant somatic recurrence and a positive cis dosage effect. Its loss explains the HIF-driven expression of CA9, ANGPTL4 and related genes.

literature.text: COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) has the best mechanistic literature in the corpus: HIF-1alpha induces its expression and mitochondrial localisation, the large majority of ccRCCs overexpress it, it increases glycolysis, and with LDHB it suppresses mitochondria-associated ferroptosis, an axis proposed as a therapeutic strategy. The evidence is preclinical, there is no approved drug, and the poor-survival claims in these papers are not reproduced by TCGA in this graph.

The literature describes CD70 as commonly overexpressed in RCC with minimal expression in normal tissue, correlated with hypoxia pathway proteins, and as a diagnostic and therapeutic target for which gallium-68 single-domain antibody radiotracers have been developed (PMID:38195301, PMID:39510586). Its reported survival association is not reproduced by TCGA in this graph.

NNMT is one of few genes where literature and data agree on adverse prognosis: a ccRCC study calls it a prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target (PMID:41399267), and selective NNMT inhibitors have been described (PMID:37523719), so a pharmacological route exists, although DepMap shows no selective dependency.

The literature on MT1G is contradictory: it is reported as lost in ccRCC and as a possible negative regulator of ferroptosis, yet high MT1G is linked to advanced stage and poorer prognosis and promotes growth and metastasis through CPT1B and lipid droplets. TCGA supports the adverse-prognosis side; a tumour-suppressor versus oncogenic role is unresolved.

SCARB1 is a literature gap: it ranks high on omics, Open Targets genetic association and the target profile, but has no literature relations in the corpus and a sentence search returned only generic ccRCC text. It should be read as a data-driven hypothesis.

external.text: Open Targets links CA9 to ccRCC only modestly [gene=CA9; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.3088], mostly through literature, with girentuximab in phase 3, and UniProt places it at the cell membrane, which suits antibody and imaging use. CA9 is not a dependency in ccRCC lines [gene=CA9; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.031], and the best PRISM compound against it is not significant [gene=CA9; type=prism_response; source=DATASET:PRISM-20Q2; padj=0.146], so the target case rests on surface expression, not on essentiality.

EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha) is the established ccRCC drug target, with belzutifan approved, and it is the only candidate near the top of the ranking with a positive DepMap selectivity signal [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3], although the adjusted q-value is not significant and only a minority of lines are dependent. Its convergence rank is modest because its RNA change is small.

The genetic anchors have the highest Open Targets associations but are not drug targets: VHL is recurrently mutated [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.483] and acts through HIF-2, and PBRM1 is the second recurrent driver [gene=PBRM1; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.362]. These tumour suppressors, with BAP1, SETD2 and KDM5C, are stratification genes and do not appear in the expression-weighted top ranks.

cells.text: CA9 is tumour-intrinsic at single-cell level: RCC cells carry almost all of its tumour transcripts [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976], and the attribution to tumour cells holds in a second single-cell dataset (Zhang 2021), although that comparison rests on only four paired donors.

EPAS1, the HIF-2 alpha driver, is mostly detected in stroma in the scRNA: the share of endothelial cells expressing it is [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=81.3], against [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=4.9] for RCC cells. A bulk EPAS1 signal is therefore not a clean tumour-cell readout, though dropout of a low-abundance transcription factor may explain part of this.

Several bulk candidates are not tumour-intrinsic. KDR is an endothelial gene [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951], and RCC cells are not among its expressing groups, so it is a microenvironment target.

CD74 and CXCR4 are immune-cell genes: macrophages carry the largest share of CD74 tumour transcripts [gene=CD74; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.436] and CD8 T cells the largest share of CXCR4 [gene=CXCR4; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=CD8_T; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.563]. They are microenvironment markers, not tumour-cell targets.

The cell source of SLC16A3 (MCT4) does not replicate across single-cell datasets: the tumour-cell share is low in Li 2022, where T and NK cells dominate [gene=SLC16A3; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.327], but high in Zhang 2021 [gene=SLC16A3; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.809]. Its tumour-intrinsic call is uncertain.

spatial.text: In paired donor pseudobulk, CA9 in tumour cells exceeds normal proximal-tubule cells [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; log2fc=7.739]. In Visium sections, high-CA9 spots are significantly enriched for RCC neighbours, the composition-corrected expresser is RCC, and macrophage neighbours are only weakly enriched. Spatial enrichment was run only for CA9.

structure.text: The CA9 AlphaFold model has moderate confidence (mean pLDDT [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56]) and its top computationally detected cavity has a volume in cubic angstroms of [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; volume_a3=126.8], with one nearby accessible lysine. This is a descriptive heuristic on a predicted monomer, not evidence of a degron, a ligase interaction or a degrader; CA9 already has antibodies and small-molecule inhibitors.

The COL23A1 model has low confidence (mean pLDDT [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91]) and only one small shallow cavity was found, with no ligand-site validation possible. If COL23A1 is pursued, an antibody is a more plausible modality than a small molecule; this too is a descriptive monomer result.

discovery.text: COL23A1 leads the tumour-cell track. It is a transmembrane collagen with few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, and in the single-cell data it is made mainly by RCC cells [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881]. The increase replicates in TCGA [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; tcga_log2fc=5.829], it survives the extrapolation to a pure tumour, vital-organ expression is low, and TCGA survival shows no adverse effect. UniProt places it at the cell membrane but surfaceome resources do not confirm it, and it has no selective dependency, no normal-tissue staining and no heterogeneity data, so it is a hypothesis for experimental validation.

RAB42 is the second tumour-track gene. It is a small GTPase with few ccRCC papers and no drug, attributed mainly to RCC cells [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627]. It replicates in TCGA and survives the purity extrapolation, but it is intracellular, so not antibody-accessible, DepMap shows no selective dependency and TCGA survival is not significant.

The stroma track is led by OLFML2A, a secreted fibroblast gene [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647] that replicates in TCGA but is also expressed in colon, and JAG2, an endothelial Notch ligand at the cell surface [gene=JAG2; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.487] with more existing literature and heart expression. Both would be microenvironment targets and neither has dependency evidence.

The immune track, which holds most of the discovery pool, is led by MILR1, a macrophage surface gene with no ccRCC papers [gene=MILR1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.841], and LILRB4, a checkpoint-like macrophage receptor [gene=LILRB4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.933]. Both are flagged infiltration-driven: their change shrinks towards zero when extrapolated to a pure tumour, so the bulk signal reflects macrophage abundance. MILR1 has an adverse TCGA survival association; bone marrow and lung expression are safety questions. All discovery genes are data-ranked hypotheses; none is a selective dependency.

validation.text: In the independent confirmatory CPTAC cohort (DIA proteome), the protein calls for NNMT, ENPP3, SCARB1 and SLC16A3 replicate in direction and significance, and so does the loss of PSAT1 [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946], PCK1 and SLC6A19. CA9 and CD70 were not tested there for lack of matched pairs, which is a gap rather than a failure. PPP1R1A stays unconfirmed [gene=PPP1R1A; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.17], and HK2 does not replicate: it is not significant and points the opposite way [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.074].

Functional layers are mostly negative. CD70 has no selective DepMap dependency [gene=CD70; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.006], nor do CA9, NNMT or SCARB1; EPAS1 is the only candidate with a positive selectivity signal, and PRISM compounds against CA9 show no significant response. 2D cell lines miss HIF-2 biology and the microenvironment, so this is absence of support, not evidence against antibody-based targets. VHL and PBRM1 are the recurrent somatic drivers. The purity check confirms the leading surface targets as tumour-intrinsic and exposes FCER1G and TYROBP as infiltration signals. Protein-adjusted kinase activity was not assessed for any leading candidate.

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting of the streams, the target profile has a stable core: SCARB1, CA9, SLC16A3, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3 and FABP6 stay in the target top ten in most draws with narrow rank intervals, whereas CYP2J2, HK2 and ANGPTL4 sit at the edge and depend on the chosen weights. In the biomarker profile only PSAT1, PCK1 and SLC6A19 are robust; ALDH6A1, PPP1R1A and NNMT have wide intervals, and SLPI, DUSP9, VWF and L1CAM are weight-dependent. In the overall convergence score only CA9 and COXFA4L2 are robustly in the top ten; SCARB1 and PIGR leave the top 25 without the genetics stream and NNMT without the literature stream.

treatment.text: CA9 expression is not associated with progression differently between the arms of IMmotion150 (atezolizumab plus bevacizumab versus sunitinib) [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.917], nor between nivolumab and everolimus in CheckMate-025 [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_nivolumab_vs_everolimus.padj=0.999]. CA9 is a tumour marker, not a treatment-selection marker.

NNMT is not associated with progression in CheckMate-025 in either arm or in the difference between them, nor in the small Choueiri nivolumab cohort, after correction. EPAS1 does not separate nivolumab from everolimus in CheckMate-025 either; the everolimus arm shows a higher response AUC but a non-significant hazard ratio, a one-arm lead only. No gene separates the arms of either trial after correction for genome-wide testing, so all treatment results are associations, not predictive markers.

subtypes.text: CA9 is a subgroup target candidate for PBRM1-mutant tumours, with higher RNA in mutants in CPTAC and TCGA but no significant protein difference after correction, and it is lower in ccB than ccA in all three datasets. It is not flagged for VHL, BAP1 or SETD2.

PSAT1 is higher in ccB than ccA in CPTAC protein, CPTAC RNA and TCGA, and higher in BAP1-mutant tumours at the RNA level but not at the protein level; it is not a subgroup target candidate. Subtype contrasts in bulk tissue can partly reflect differences in immune and stromal infiltration between subgroups.

adc.text: CD70 is the best-placed conjugate candidate among the leading genes: it is a surface protein (UniProt: cell-membrane ligand of CD27) with no vital-organ enrichment in the GTEx proteome and an antibody-drug conjugate suitability rank of [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; rank=3] among the genes scored. HPA staining is missing, so normal-tissue safety is untested by immunohistochemistry, and clinical anti-CD70 agents make it a known target.

SCARB1 is a high-confidence surface protein, but it stains at the highest level in the adrenal gland and its proteome tissue-specificity is enriched there [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.08]; only a small share of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors. It ranks first in the target profile but is a weak conjugate or radioligand candidate.

ENPP3 is a known conjugate target (AGS-16C3F reached phase 2) whose protein is up in tumour [gene=ENPP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.544], with a surface call and no vital-organ protein enrichment, but HPA staining is at the top level in duodenum and normal kidney, so on-target off-tumour kidney exposure is a concern. CA9 serves as a control: a known target with top-level stomach staining and incomplete tumour-cell coverage in the weakest donors.

immune.text: FCGR3A is almost entirely made by immune cells in tumours and tracks the immune score closely, so its tumour increase reflects infiltration, typical of immune-hot tumours, and it is a microenvironment marker rather than a tumour-intrinsic target.

FCER1G looks strongly up in bulk, but it tracks purity inversely [gene=FCER1G; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_purity_rho=-0.692] and the change shrinks when extrapolated to a pure tumour [gene=FCER1G; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.061]; its signal is immune infiltration, as for TYROBP and the immune-track discovery genes.

NNMT serves as a non-immune control: its tumour transcripts come almost entirely from non-immune cells and correlate only weakly with CD8 T cells and the immune score, so its signal is not an infiltration artefact and it is not an immune target.

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge converge on CA9, CD70 and NNMT, and on COXFA4L2 for omics and literature. They disagree in three places. The literature's prognostic claims for CA9, CD70 and COXFA4L2 are not reproduced by TCGA survival in this graph. For ABAT, a pan-cancer paper reports poor prognosis in KIRC while TCGA associates high ABAT with better survival. EPAS1 is the approved drug target but in the scRNA it is detected mostly in endothelium, and the cell source of SLC16A3 changes between single-cell datasets.

Classifying the candidates: CA9, CD70 and ENPP3 are surface targets for antibodies, conjugates or imaging, with CA9 also a diagnostic biomarker; NNMT is both a prognostic biomarker and a metabolic target candidate; SCARB1 and SLC16A3 are target candidates with open questions (safety and cell source); COXFA4L2 is a mechanistic biomarker; PSAT1, PCK1, SLC6A19, ALDOB and ALDH6A1 are tissue-loss biomarkers; and VHL, PBRM1 and EPAS1 define the mechanism, with EPAS1 the one established drug target.

targets.rationale: Top of the overall ranking and robust in the target profile: tumour-intrinsic surface antigen, replicated in TCGA and in a second single-cell dataset, with clinical antibodies and PET imaging. Not prognostic, not a dependency, and stomach staining is a safety concern for cytotoxic modalities; best as an imaging, delivery and diagnostic target.

Robust in the target profile; tumour-intrinsic surface protein with no vital-organ enrichment in the GTEx proteome and clinical anti-CD70 agents, so the cleanest conjugate candidate here. Not tested in the confirmatory cohort and not a dependency.

Robust in the target profile and the only leading candidate where omics, literature and TCGA survival agree on adverse prognosis; protein replicates in the confirmatory cohort, the signal is non-immune, and selective inhibitors exist. Cytosolic, no clinical drug and no selective dependency.

Robust in the target profile; tumour-intrinsic membrane enzyme whose protein replicates in the confirmatory cohort, with a conjugate that reached phase 2. Staining in normal kidney and duodenum is the main concern, and it has no prognostic signal.

First and most robust in the target profile and replicated in the confirmatory cohort, but placed below CA9, CD70, NNMT and ENPP3 because its protein is enriched in the adrenal gland, coverage of tumour cells is low in some donors, it has no literature support in the corpus and its overall rank depends on the genetics stream.

Robust second in the overall ranking with the strongest mechanistic literature (HIF-driven mitochondrial adaptation, ferroptosis suppression) and a tumour-intrinsic change replicated in TCGA; a biomarker rather than a target because it has no specific drug, no dependency and no prognostic signal in TCGA.

Robust in the target profile and protein replicates in the confirmatory cohort, but its cell source changes between single-cell datasets, so the tumour-intrinsic call is uncertain, and it has no drug or dependency.

Established mechanism-level target with approved belzutifan and the only positive DepMap selectivity signal near the top of the ranking; ranked low numerically because its RNA change is small, and detected mostly in endothelium in the scRNA.
Most robust gene in the biomarker profile; its protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort, and it differs between ccA and ccB subtypes.
Robust in the biomarker profile; protein loss and both measured phosphosites replicate in the confirmatory cohort.
Robust in the biomarker profile; protein loss and all measured phosphosites replicate in the confirmatory cohort, from a modest number of pairs.

Third in the overall ranking; proximal-tubule lineage-loss gene whose remaining expression tracks survival in TCGA, so a diagnostic and prognostic marker. Not robust in the biomarker profile, and lost genes cannot be inhibited.

Exploratory: top tumour-cell discovery gene, made mainly by RCC cells, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust with no clinical drug; main limitation is that its surface location, normal-tissue staining and dependency are unconfirmed.
Exploratory: second tumour-cell discovery gene, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust; main limitation is that it is intracellular, has no selective dependency and no survival signal.

limitations.text: FABP6 is robust in the target profile but is left out of the targets list because no specialist profiled it (no cell source, safety or confirmatory data in this run).
HK2 ranks in the target top ten but is left out of the targets list because its protein change does not replicate in the confirmatory cohort.
PIGR is robust in the overall top ten but its rank depends on the genetics stream, it is lost in tumour rather than gained, and no specialist profiled it; it is not listed.
Protein-adjusted kinase activity was not assessed for the leading candidates, and STRING interaction context was not retrieved.
DepMap and PRISM use 2D cell lines, which miss HIF-2 biology and the tumour microenvironment; absence of a dependency is not evidence against antibody-based targets.
CA9 and CD70 were not tested in the confirmatory cohort for lack of matched pairs; this is a gap, not a failure to replicate.

The literature corpus is a few hundred ccRCC abstracts, often reusing TCGA data, so literature agreement is not fully independent of the omics streams; the PubMed connector was not available in this run.
The single-cell data cover a small number of donors, the second dataset adds only four paired donors, and spatial enrichment was run only for CA9.
Structural cavity scores describe predicted monomers and are not evidence of degrons, ligase interactions or degraders.
Discovery genes are data-ranked hypotheses: novel means few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, and none has a selective dependency or functional evidence in this analysis.
Treatment associations come from two modest trials; no gene separates the arms of either trial after correction.
Passing the automatic checks establishes evidence linkage and numeric bindings, not complete scientific validation.
